_README: Read by bundle/assert-sp-no-data-select.py. Each entry records ONE grant that
gives the app's service principal read access to the governed data schema, and
that has been examined and accepted anyway.
An entry needs granted_on, privilege, via_principal, reason, owner and
review_by. Anything missing means the entry covers nothing -- a half-filled
exception is how a file like this becomes an allowlist. Past its review_by an
entry STOPS covering its finding and the check fails, on purpose: 'we decided
not to fix this' must not decay into 'nobody has looked since August'.
owner IS A ROLE, NOT A PERSON. This file is published to the public repository,
so an @databricks.com address here is a disclosure and check-mirror-leaks.sh is
right to stop it. Name the role that answers for the decision.
Do not add an entry to make a red check green. The first two below describe a
grant on the CATALOG, which is shared estate; a grant made directly to the
service principal is ours to close, and recording it here instead would be
using this file to look away.
THE THIRD ENTRY IS SCHEMA-LEVEL, which the paragraph above says is ours. Read
its reason before adding another like it: it is accepted because revoking it
would remove the finding and change no access at all -- `account users` still
reaches every table in this schema through the catalog entries above -- so the
revoke is housekeeping with a review date on it rather than a fix somebody is
waiting for. An entry whose removal WOULD close access does not belong here.

exceptions.reason: The shared demo catalog grants ALL_PRIVILEGES to `account users`, and every service principal in the account is in that group, so the app SP inherits read on this schema and every table in it. Revoking the app SP's own explicit grant was tried on 2026-08-17 and did NOT close the access, which is the finding this exception exists to keep visible. Closing it properly means a catalog-level revoke affecting several hundred schemas owned by dozens of other people, which is not this project's call to make. The control that actually holds is at runtime, not in the grant: the agent reads governed tables as the signed-in caller and agent/execution_identity.py refuses before the model call if the identity does not match. This exception records an inherited capability that is not exercised; it does not license exercising it.

The same `account users` grant on the shared catalog, spelled as SELECT alongside ALL_PRIVILEGES. Recorded separately because the check matches one privilege per entry and a wildcard would also cover a privilege nobody has looked at. Same reasoning and same review date as the ALL_PRIVILEGES entry above: the app service principal INHERITS this read through its membership of `account users`, so revoking the principal's own grant does not close it and never did. A green check on this deployment therefore does NOT mean the service principal cannot read the governed data. It means the one control that actually holds is the runtime one -- the agent reads as the signed-in caller and agent/execution_identity.py refuses before the model call on an identity mismatch.

WHY THE SCHEMA IS SPELLED OUT AND NOT `${schema}`: this file has two readers and they disagree. bundle/assert-sp-no-data-select.py resolves both `${catalog}` and `${schema}`; bundle/drift-check.py resolves only `${catalog}`, so the parameterised form matched for one and pointed at nothing for the other -- which read as 'no exception records this finding' AND 'this record describes access that is gone', from the same file, in the same run. A literal one reader has to be told about beats a placeholder that silently means different things to each. The publication rewrites this schema name the same way it rewrites it in databricks.yml, so it is not a disclosure; if the schema is ever renamed, both checks fail loudly rather than passing quietly. THE MECHANISM, as Unity Catalog reports it rather than as it is usually described: `account users` holds SELECT on this schema, and the app service principal is in that group because every service principal in the account is. Unity Catalog names the schema as the securable this one was granted ON, so it is a THIRD path, alongside the SELECT and ALL_PRIVILEGES the two entries above inherit from the catalog. It is therefore partly ours -- we own the schema and could revoke it -- and it is recorded rather than revoked because revoking it would remove this finding and change no access whatsoever: the catalog grant reaches all fifteen securables in this schema on its own, so a reader who took the revoke as a fix would be wrong in the direction that matters. WHAT A GREEN CHECK MEANS AFTER THIS, stated because the opposite reading is the risk: it does NOT mean the app service principal cannot read the governed data. It can, by three paths, all recorded. The check asserts something narrower and still worth having -- that no UNRECORDED path exists, and that each recorded one is re-examined by its review date. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: a revoke of `account users` on the shared catalog, which belongs to another owner and covers every schema in that estate, or moving this schema to a catalog that does not grant `account users` at all. Both were considered and deprioritised on 2026-08-17; neither is a change this project can make alone. WHY THE EXPOSURE IS NARROWER THAN THE GRANT: the capability exists at the platform level and the application no longer exercises it. The agent reads governed tables as the signed-in caller, and on 2026-08-17 the three remaining ways it could have read them as itself were removed -- the gate that returned None for a version logged without a user auth policy, the construction of data tools on the passthrough client, and the default that built a workspace client when handed none. Verified rather than assumed: the version now serving was logged AFTER those removals, from a commit that contains them, with the user-authorization policy recorded on its logging run. This exception records an inherited capability that is not exercised; it does not license exercising it, and the runtime control in agent/execution_identity.py is what holds.
